title: Adaptive Shrinkage with a Nonparametric Bayesian Lasso
text: R package bnplasso (developer’s version) implements Nonparametric Bayesian Lasso described Marin et al. (2026). main routine package, bnplasso_lm(), returns object S3 class, "lmBayes", supported various methods print(), summary(), plot(), fitted(), residuals(), coef(), predict(), allowing users quickly visualize, evaluate, analyze output familiar fashion. function bnplasso_lm() can also implement Bayesian Lasso (Park Casella, 2008) Bayesian adaptive Lasso (Leng et al., 2014).

title: Adaptive Shrinkage with a Nonparametric Bayesian Lasso
text: First, let’s start loading packages required bnplasso necessary illustrative example. Next, let’s generate synthetic predictors. , training set size 250 (n.train), held-set size 2000 (n.test). covariate space 200 dimensions (p), covariate vector drawn multivariate normal distribution mean zero AR(1) covariance matrix, correlation parameter 0.7 (rho). Now, generate model parameters. , intercept term equal ten (mu), residual standard deviation one (sigma), vector regression coefficients generated way 10% entries nonzero (beta). Finally, let’s generate responses. can easily apply nonparametric Bayesian Lasso (Marin et al., 2025+) data function bnplasso_lm(). Note supplying design matrix response vector. user-supplied hyperparameters provided, bnplasso_lm() function attempt automatically determine appropriate values hyperparameters. said, different applications may require different tailored prior specifications. method summary() provides information model fit. includes details function call, well posterior mean, posterior standard deviation, various posterior quantiles, MCMC effective sample size model parameters. method plot() produces various model diagnostics plots, including posterior predictive checks residual diagnostics.   One can also extract individual chains containing posterior draws model parameters. instance, let’s extract plot chains intercept, beta_1, beta_200.    Note chains centered around true parameter values exhibit good mixing! useful class-specific methods include: can also visualize posterior co-clustering probabilities, .e., posterior probabilities two regression coefficients clustered together.  Note first 20 regression coefficients (nonzero) clustered together large probability, remaining 180 (zero) also clustered together large probability. , nonparametric Bayesian Lasso accurately performing variable selection. desired, one can also obtain point estimate partition regression coefficients. default, function get.partition() employs variation information loss function Wade Ghahramani (2018); however, users can also employ Binder loss function. One can visualize partition function coclust.point().  also possible perform --sample predictions using method predict(). result matrix size n.draws--n.test, column contains posterior predictive draws one points wish predict.  instance, plots show posterior predictive distribution along actual response values first last points held-set. Given held-set, one can evaluate --sample predictive performance model using expected log point-wise predictive density (elppd) function elppd(). held-set available, one can estimate model fit using functions psis.loo() widely.aic(), compute Pareto-smoothed importance sampling leave-one-information criterion (PSIS-LOO) Watanabe–Akaike information criterion (WAIC), Vehtari et al. (2017). Additional guidelines help pages using package functions available . Source code data reproduce results Marin et al. (2026) available https://github.com/marinsantiago/bnplasso-examples.
code: library(mvtnorm) p <- 200 rho <- 0.7 n.train <- 250 n.test <- 2000  set.seed(1) Sigma.x <- rho^abs(matrix(1:p - 1, p, p, byrow = TRUE) - (1:p - 1)) X.train <- rmvnorm(n.train, rep(0, p), Sigma.x) X.test <- rmvnorm(n.test, rep(0, p), Sigma.x) mu <- 10 sigma <- 1 beta <- c(rep(5, 20), rep(0, 180)) set.seed(1) y.train <- as.vector(mu + X.train %*% beta + rnorm(n.train, 0, sigma)) y.test <- as.vector(mu + X.test %*% beta + rnorm(n.test, 0, sigma)) set.seed(1) out.bnp <- bnplasso::bnplasso_lm(X.train, y.train) summary(out.bnp) LINEAR REGRESSION MODEL   Call details:  a = 0.1 b = 4e-05 n.obs = 250 n.preds = 200 n.draws = 4000 (after burn-in and thinning) elapsed = 1.761656  Coefficients:             mean    sd   2.5%    25%    50%    75%  97.5%     n_eff Intercept 10.022 0.063  9.899  9.979 10.022 10.065 10.144 4000.0000 beta_1     4.934 0.089  4.765  4.875  4.933  4.994  5.110 4000.0000 beta_2     5.111 0.108  4.903  5.036  5.112  5.184  5.324 4000.0000 beta_3     5.004 0.111  4.787  4.929  5.004  5.078  5.229 4000.0000 beta_4     5.116 0.107  4.903  5.043  5.117  5.190  5.325 3776.8363 beta_5     4.736 0.104  4.532  4.667  4.734  4.806  4.940 3546.9278 ⋮ plot(out.bnp) plot(out.bnp$post.mu, type = "l", ylab = "", main = "mu") plot(out.bnp$post.beta[,1], type = "l", ylab = "", main = "beta_1") plot(out.bnp$post.beta[,200], type = "l", ylab = "", main = "beta_200") print(out.bnp) fitted(out.bnp) residuals(out.bnp) coef(out.bnp) bnplasso::coclust.probs(out.bnp$post.clust_idx) part <- bnplasso::get.partition(out.bnp$post.clust_idx) bnplasso::coclust.point(part) pprd <- predict(out.bnp, X.test) dim(pprd) 4000 2000 plot(density(pprd[,1]), lwd = 3, xlab = "", ylab = "", "y_test.1") abline(v = y.test[1], col = 2, lwd = 3, lty = 2) legend("topright", c("Predicted", "Actual"), lwd = 3, col = 1:2, lty = 1:2)  plot(density(pprd[,2000]), lwd = 3, xlab = "", ylab = "", "y_test.2000") abline(v = y.test[2000], col = 2, lwd = 3, lty = 2) legend("topright", c("Predicted", "Actual"), lwd = 3, col = 1:2, lty = 1:2) bnplasso::elppd(out.bnp, X.test, y.test) -1.503273 bnplasso::psis.loo(out.bnp) bnplasso::widely.aic(out.bnp) 710.662 See Moran et al. (2019) details. options either "independent" "conjugate". provided, function attempt determine appropriate prior. max_iters positive integer corresponding total number MCMC iterations. Default 10000. burn_in positive integer corresponding number draws discarded burn-. smaller max_iters. Default 20000. thin positive integer specifying period saving samples. title: bnplasso 0.3.0
text: efficient implementation underlying Gibbs sampler used generate random draws posterior distribution model. new implementation roughly 6x faster previous implementation. Renamed functions functions’ arguments sake clarity. instance, blasso.lm() renamed blasso_lm(). Similarly, prior renamed shrinkage_prior polya renamed polya_urn_sampler. package now support double point precision. Latest version available GitHub.

title: bnplasso 0.2.2
text: package now includes dedicated routine, bnplasso.spm(), implements sparse normal-means problem. routine returns object S3 class, "spmBayes", supported various class-specific methods. internal functionality improvements. Archived GitHub version: marinsantiago/bnplasso@dee47cd

title: bnplasso 0.2.1
text: package now includes functions psis.loo() widely.aic(), compute Pareto-smoothed importance sampling leave-one-information criterion (PSIS-LOO) Watanabe–Akaike information criterion (WAIC), respectively. Archived GitHub version: marinsantiago/bnplasso@6adfa6d

title: bnplasso 0.2.0
text: functions blasso.lm() balasso.lm() merged function, bnplasso.lm(). new argument, prior, introduced bnplasso.lm(), specifies type shrinkage prior employed. options : (1) nonparametric Bayesian Lasso prior (default), (2) Bayesian Lasso prior, (3) Bayesian adaptive Lasso prior. bnplasso.lm() function now supports single-precision floating-point calculations certain internal routines via float argument. default, function still uses double point precision. default, bnplasso.lm() function now includes intercept term regression function. bnplasso.lm() function now returns log-likelihood observation MCMC iteration. user-supplied hyperparameters provided, bnplasso.lm() function now attempt automatically determine appropriate values hyperparameters. package now includes function get.partition(), recovers partition regression coefficients induced nonparametric Bayesian Lasso. package now includes functions coclust.probs() coclust.point(), compute visualize matrices co-clustering probabilities co-clustering point estimates, respectively. internal functionality improvements, including better handling numerical instabilities memory management. Archived GitHub version: marinsantiago/bnplasso@4cf966b
